Many people got very highhhh scoreeee!!!!

omg! I need to work much harder!!
Yay, I got 81 in final, however mean: 78, median: 84

Midterm involve the content from lecture 1 to 9 and final involve the remaining lectures only. Open book&notes for both exams.

You need to understand all of the concepts clearly in order to get good score. The scores in the exams are distributed unevenly.

I heard that the exam papers are almost the same for every year. So it benefit those who got past paper a lot. Don't enroll in this course if you are a person like me or else C range is waiting for you.

Btw, what I want to tell about final exam is that there is a 6 score question that ask you to write 500 words essay on how material change the world. 6 score is too low but it is worth to prepare the essay before final exam so that you can directly copy it during the exam. sections.content: A comprehensive intro to material science. Including the general topics in materials while highlighting Crystal Structure and Phase Diagram (for metalic arrangement). I learnt chemistry in high-school but most of the knowledge is new to me. Feel free to try this as your common core course if you want to learn more about material science, strongly recommend to engineering students.
sections.teaching:
Prof. Shao does have accent, therefore requires students to preview some of the terminologes. (Believe me, this really helps if you want to understand what he says!)
His teaching is a little too brief hence you have to go through the textbook. Good news is that he and TAs will answer your questions so that understand the knowledge is not that hard.
sections.grading:
My midterm:100 My final:98.
Anecdote says the paper for each year is almost the same. But I can't  confirm.
In terms of the difficulty, you can get beautiful grade if you understan d the concept, the problems are some basic applications of what discussed in class.
Both exams allow cheat sheet. I print all the slides before exam however the effectiveness is limited. Strongly recommend to solve your problems before exam, rote memorize is not that useful.
sections.workload:
Workload is tiny tiny hard for me. I seldom read through the textbook for a single course but for this course I did. The character of this course is that some techniques and concepts is complex at first, you may spend a lot time to make full comprehesion. But after you get the essence, homework and exam questions are like piece of  cake.
Generally speaking, the workload is fair enough for 3 cre.

sections.content:
The content is very technical and requires advanced knowledge of Physics and Chemistry. There are a lot of formulas and complex calculations in this course, which means you need to have a solid mathematical sense.

Although the content is a bit difficult, it doesn't mean the exam is difficult since he skips the most difficult part of the exam.
sections.teaching:
Honestly speaking, the professor has a strong mainland accent and it is hard to immediately understand what he said. You need to review his zoom recording.

However, he is friendly and willing to answer students' questions. He is easy-going and approachable.

There are four TAs in this course. Wang Yian is quite nice. However, there are two assistants who are a little bit lazy as they always messed up with the format of the assignments and caused a lot of confusion among the students.

The professor has a heavy accent that may take some time to get used to.

sections.grading:
For reference, i got a 3 in dse chemistry and 4 in physics.

2 grading schemes

With presentation:
Homework: 10%
Midterm: 30%
Final exam: 40%
Presentation: 20%

Without presentation:
Homework: 10%
Midterm: 40%
Final exam: 50%

The presentation will be done in the last week or two of the lectures, either solo or in a group of 2. You will need to introduce a material and its applications.

My grades:
Homework: full
Midterm: 85/100, mean 72
Presentation: did not do
Final: 82.5/100, mean 78
Overall: 85.25
Grading: B

I've heard that you need an overall score of at least 91 to get an A range in this semester. The grading is very harsh. Maybe it's because that the mean this semester is higher than normal.

Midterm is mostly calculations while final has more essay-type questions. I find midterm a lot easier than final so do your best to score high in midterm.
sections.workload:
The wordload is acceptable.

There is weekly homework but you will get full mark once you handed in, so please remember to do them.

There will be exam highlights before midterm and final, just attend those lectures and revise accordingly. I find the textbook very boring so i just rewatch all the lecture videos for revision.

Textbook questions are usually not in the same format as the questions that appear in the exam, so there is no need to do them unless you aim high. Reviewing homework questions will be very helpful as the format is similar to that of the exam.

The exam is open book and notes.

sections.content: Although it's an "introductory" course, the content is fairly complex and requires a lot of reading of the textbook to understand. Even though the PowerPoint slides cover everything, they only 'introduce' the content, to some extent, but to fully grasp the concepts, reading the textbook is necessary.
sections.teaching: The accent is hard to understand, hence I only attended a few lectures.
sections.grading: The grading is pretty harsh, I got mean and still C+. The mean is not extremely hard to achieve, but unfortunately, I guess I didn't revise enough. The exam is an open book and notes, however, you cannot use Wi-Fi.
sections.workload: Fairly low workload, in terms of assignments. There will be 10 homeworks worth 1% each, and thus 10% of the total grade. Apart from that, studying for the course requires a lot of time and concentration.

sections.content:
Midterm:
Lecture 1 introduction (skip得)
• material --> tool/weapon
• 唔同時代(stone,bronze,iron...)
• metals/ceramics(crystalline)/glasses(amorphous)  
Lecture 2 Atomic structure and bonding (讀過chem skip得)
• Avogadro's number = 6.02^23 (1mol=6.02^23個/1打=12個)
•  Ionic Bond** 
   (Coor. Number, r/R ratio, electrostatic force Fc)
• Covalent Bond
• Metallic Bond
• Van der Waals' F
Lecture 3 Crystal structure
• Unit cell (識SC,FCC,BCC,HCP)
• 計a, APF(寫定d公式)
• 留意MX2 structure(例CaF2)
["rCa2+ + rF- = 1/4 diagonal"]
["diagonal = sqrt(3)a"]
Lecture 4 Lattice position and plane
• 玩Vector
• linear&plane density
(寫定每個最(最唔)dense個條&plane)
• 識畫plane
(1. plane
2. find intercept(1/plane) )
Lecture 5 X-ray diffraction 
• Bragg eqn [nλ=2dsinθ]
• Interplanar Spacing(面面距離)
• Diffraction Rules (表:自己寫定所有組合)
Steps:
1. 查表--> hkl (每個structure頭三個hkl)
2. hkl & a --> d (面面距離)
3. λ & d --> θ (Bragg angle) (Bragg eqn)
4. 2θ (peak angle)
• Scherrer eqn(β用'radian')[angle*180/pi],θ普通度數(Bragg angle)
Lecture 6 Crystal defects
• Hume-Rothery rules
1. atomic radii diff. <15%
2. same structure
3. EN diff. <30%
4. same Valence e(#最外層電子)
• Point defects
• linear/Planar defects
Lecture 7 Diffusion
• Arrhenius equation(讀過chem唔陌生)
-2個temp,2個rate:Find Ea(呢個course叫 Q)
-然後Find某個temp rate
Lecture 8 Mechanical properties I 
• σ stress[F/A], ε strain[ (L-L0)/L0 ]
• E Elasticity(Young's modulus)(直綫個段斜率)
• Y.S Yield strength (係0.2%strain,拉條E斜率綫)
• Tensile strength (條curve最高點)
• εfailure (curve終點拉條E斜率綫落去)
-> Ductility (εfailure * 100)
• poisson's ratio & shear stress
Lecture 9 Mechanical properties II
• MOR
• Griffith crack model(用crack解釋ceramics tensile &compress現象)
• Resolved shear stress
• Hardness BHN formula(D,d in mm)
• Creep stress,rate (Arrhenius eqn)
Lecture 10 Thermal behaviour
• Thermal Expansion
• Thermal conductivity
-> factor affect
• Thermal shock
->mechanism:
1. Thermal expansion
2. Significant temp gradient.
================================
Final:
Lecture 11-13 Phase diagram I,II,III
• Degree of freedom
• 準備好唔同structure diagram(Eutectic, Eutectoid)
• Lever Rule
• draw phase diagram
Lecture 14-15 Heat treatment I,II
• Nucleation and growth rate
• TTT-diagram
• Quench rate
• %microstructure / time required
• Tempering(Martempering,Austempering)
log scale:
0.1 0.2...1
1 2 3 4...10
10 20 30...100
• Hardenability
• Ppt Hardening(how?), Cold work
Lecture 16 Structure materials-metals
• 整理個表出黎(知道alloy好多方面應用)
Lecture 17 Polymers and composits(讀chem輕鬆d)
• rms length & extended length
 Lecture 18-19 Electronic materials-conductors, insulators and superconductors(讀過chem,phy容易理解dd)
• V=IR, R=Pl/A
• conductivity(=1/resistivity) (=nqu)
• Why high conduct.(1 atom:>1 free e)
• Energy lvl & band
• fermi function
• fermi level(Ef) = Egap/2 (except p/n type)

{Insulator}
• Capacitor(Capacitance)
E = Vd / V=Ed
ε = kε0
Charge den. D = εE = Q/A
Capacitance C = Q/V

{Semiconductor}
Intrinsic:pure
extrinsic:n/p type
• how Ef changed?
• charge carrier
 非重點(理解下,睇下例題用公式,直抄notes)
 重點(一定/大幾率考)

sections.content:
This course focuses on basic knowledge of material science. At the core, the topics try to give an understanding of the relationship between the atomic structure of a material and its macroscopic properties. Some lectures, like L7, get pretty technical but it is not that important to memorize all those details for the exam. Solving the exam and HW problems does not require complex math. Overall, the material is very interesting and good for Common Core.

Syllabus:
L1 - Introduction
L2 - Atomic Structure and Bonding
L3 - Crystal Structure
L4 - Lattice Positions, Directions and Planes
L5 - X-Ray Diffraction
L6 - Crystal Defects
L7 - Diffusion (Solid State)
L8 - Mechanical Properties I
L9 - Mechanical Properties II
L10 - Thermal Behavior
L11/12 - Phase Diagrams I
L13 - Phase Diagrams II
L14 - Heat Treatment I
L15 - Heat Treatment II
L16 - Structure Materials: Metals
L17 - Structure Materials: Polymers and Composites
L18 - Electronic Materials: Metals and Superconductors
L19 - Electronic Materials: Semiconductors and Insulators
L20 - Materials for Batteries (does not come in textbook)
sections.teaching: Prof. Shao has a strong accent, but after some time he is not so difficult to understand. The lecture notes have the key points, but he explains things a lot more in depth, so it is important to attend lectures. He is very polite and responds to questions and emails very quick. He also had an office hour every week to talk with him on zoom.
sections.grading:
After the midterm, we can choose whether we want to make a presentation on some material science topic or not. Doing so changes the grading scheme:

Grading scheme (without presentation):
- Homework: 10%
- Midterm: 40%
- Final: 50%

Grading scheme (with presentation):
- Homework: 10%
- Midterm: 30%
- Presentation: 20%
- Final: 40%

The exams were open-book, open-notes. The midterm had more calculations and the final had more essay-type questions. The final was split in two parts. One of them was only about phase diagrams, so it is very important to understand how they work. Many of the question types were already discussed in lectures or tutorials, and they give enough time to do everything correctly.
sections.workload: There is one HW per week, each with 2-3 short problems. Submission was made via Canvas.

去到Mechanical properties開始到Heat treatment就比較難，因為係全新嘅concept同埋真係要上堂先會明白到，然後structure materials，batteries果啲有chem底易明。Conductors果啲都係比較informative啲，但concept都係比較難。

就cc course黎講呢一科學嘅野比較technical，有好多野都係有個知字。讀呢一科要抱住個心態係：就算我唔知果樣野係咩黎，當左佢係啱先，都唔好了解太多背後發生緊乜事。因為呢科好多野對正常人黎講都係陌生野，而呢科好多時候都用難嘅concept去解釋一啲現象而又唔會解釋太多，就好似semiconductor入面個fermi level咁，你要識得代公式果啲，但其實唔太知佢係乜黎，點解會有。

書見前幾年有review話買左好有用，所以我都買左書，但唔知係咩原因，書寫嘅野好難理解，同埋又長又悶。所以都係上齊Lecture最緊要，當然考試果陣有書係有幫助嘅，但你事前要熟本書嘅內容又係幾哂時間啦。

特別留意"stress", "strain"呢啲字佢讀得好似，"concentration"會變"contration"咁樣。
呢一科嘅lecture notes係好短同精簡，基本上唔上堂係無可能睇得明佢講乜，佢上堂果陣會講一啲mt, final學生成日唔識答嘅問題，有上堂基本上可以攞哂分。

sections.content: Content is easily understandable and it is interesting never learned about materials science before.
sections.teaching: Honestly no need of attending the class since the professor just reads the slides plus the lecture is recorded and can be watched on canvas. Professor's lecture note is somewhat useful and enough to prepare fore exams.
sections.grading: The presentation is optional, but recommend to do it since it raises the grade a lot if you have not done well in midterm exam. Both the exams are open-book and most of the questions are calculations.
sections.workload: There are some calculation homework every week but a few questions. Not much to study since the exams are in open-book. Only need to work hard for presentation.
